headline: PILOT MOUNTAIN TUNGSTEN PFS DROPS TODAY — FIRST NEW U.S. TUNGSTEN MINE STUDY IN 15 YEARS, BACKED BY $6.2M DoD TITLE III GRANT (NYSE.A:GMTL)
snippet: Guardian Metal Resources PLC (NYSE.A:GMTL | LON:GMET | OTCQB:GMTLF) is releasing its Pre-Feasibility Study for the Pilot Mountain Tungsten Project in Nevada today, June 30, 2026 — marking the first detailed economic assessment of what would be the first new domestically mined U.S. tungsten operation in over 15 years. The PFS is supported by a $6.2 million Defense Production Act Title III investment from the U.S. Department of War and was developed with Samuel Engineering; a live investor presentation is scheduled for July 1 to walk through the mine plan, processing strategy, and development economics. Pilot Mountain sits alongside Tempiute — formerly America's largest producing tungsten operation — giving Guardian two co-flagship Nevada tungsten assets at a moment when the Pentagon has designated tungsten a critical strategic mineral.

headline: NEW FOUND GOLD GRADUATES TO TSX — QUEENSWAY JUNIOR LEAVES TSXV WITH SYMBOL NFGC RESERVED, DELISTING FROM VENTURE TO FOLLOW (TSX:NFGC)
source_name: Newsfile Corp. / New Found Gold Corp.
snippet: New Found Gold Corp. (TSXV:NFG | NYSE American:NFGC) received conditional approval on June 29, 2026 to graduate its common shares to the Toronto Stock Exchange, with the ticker symbol 'NFGC' reserved to align with its NYSE American listing — subject to fulfilling all TSX requirements by September 14, 2026. The graduation represents a corporate milestone for the operator of the Queensway Gold Project in Newfoundland, home to the high-grade Lotto and Iceberg zones; concurrent delisting from the TSXV will follow TSX trading commencement. CEO Keith Boyle noted the move provides the company with greater visibility and liquidity as it advances one of Canada's most-watched gold exploration programs.

headline: BLIND GOLD-SILVER VEIN FOUND 30M BELOW COVER IN BC — GEOPHYSICS MODEL CRACKS OPEN 3TS DISTRICT AT BALROG TARGET (TSXV:IGO)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Independence Gold Corp.
snippet: Independence Gold Corp. (TSXV:IGO | OTCQB:IEGCF) announced June 29, 2026 the discovery of a new gold-silver vein system at the Balrog Target within its 35,486-hectare 3Ts Gold and Silver Project in central British Columbia — the first target successfully tested via a district-scale structural model built from a 2025 airborne geophysical survey. Balrog is located approximately 200 metres west of the Johnny Vein (2.51 g/t Au / 19.73 g/t Ag), is entirely concealed beneath approximately 30 metres of glacial till, and was identified with no surface exposure — demonstrating that the structural model unlocks previously inaccessible portions of the 3Ts district where additional arcuate and radial targets are being drilled now with assays pending.

headline: FIRST DRILL TURNS AT ANDREI — ENDURO TARGETS 4KM CU-AU PORPHYRY IN GOLDEN TRIANGLE, NEXT-DOOR TO GALORE CREEK AND KSM (TSXV:ENDR)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Enduro Metals Corporation
snippet: Enduro Metals Corporation (TSXV:ENDR) commenced its first-ever diamond drill program at the Andrei copper-gold porphyry target on June 29, 2026, within the company's 688 km² Newmont Lake Project in the Golden Triangle of northwest British Columbia — testing a combined 4-kilometre chargeability and magnetic anomaly that lies at the convergence of structural corridors shared with Galore Creek (Newmont-Teck JV) and KSM (Seabridge Gold). The 3,000-metre Phase One program targets the largest component of a 14-kilometre magnetic-high trend and represents inaugural drilling of what could be a district-scale porphyry system in a camp that has already produced several world-class copper-gold discoveries.

headline: GOLD SETTLES Q2 AT $4,028 — DOWN 10% IN JUNE, SILVER BELOW $59 IN WORST MONTHLY CLOSE FOR PRECIOUS METALS SINCE 2022
snippet: Gold closed the second quarter of 2026 near US$4,028 per ounce — down approximately 10.5% in June and roughly 28% from the January all-time high of $5,589 — as markets priced in three Federal Reserve rate hikes following Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish debut, while a U.S.-Iran ceasefire announced June 15 simultaneously stripped gold of its safe-haven premium. Silver underperformed further, falling below $59 per ounce for a monthly decline exceeding 20% — its sharpest June selloff in at least a decade — with both metals recording their worst quarterly close since the 2022 rate-shock reset. Despite the price action, central bank buying remained robust at 244 metric tonnes in Q1 2026, maintaining the sovereign demand floor that has characterized the current bull cycle.

headline: RECORD 45% OF CENTRAL BANKS PLAN TO ADD GOLD IN NEXT 12 MONTHS — WGC SURVEY SHOWS RESERVE MANAGERS UNDETERRED BY $4,000 LEVEL
snippet: The World Gold Council's 2026 Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey, covered by Money Metals on June 25, found that a record 45% of the 76 central bank respondents plan to increase their gold holdings over the next 12 months — the highest share since the WGC began tracking reserve manager intentions. With Q1 2026 central bank purchases reaching 244 metric tonnes — exceeding both the prior quarter and the five-year quarterly average — the WGC data underscores that institutional accumulation is structurally independent of spot price levels, providing a demand floor that has historically limited the depth of gold corrections even during significant macro headwinds.

headline: TERBIUM SURGES 22.8% IN JUNE, NdPr UP 10% — HEAVY RARE EARTH RECOVERY HINGES ON CHINA'S H2 MOFCOM QUOTA DECISION
snippet: Mainrich International's June 2026 rare earth market update documents a sharp reversal following May's correction: terbium rose 22.8% to US$969.69/kg, the NdPr alloy benchmark gained 10.0% to US$109.55/kg, and praseodymium metal climbed 13.9% to US$124.88/kg — with the FOB premium for terbium over Chinese domestic pricing reaching approximately US$436/kg as Western buyers price in ongoing structural supply scarcity. The pivotal near-term variable is China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology H2 2026 rare earth quota announcement: tightening would extend the current recovery; an expansion could cap it and trigger a further correction across the NdPr complex.

headline: COPPER CLOSES Q2 AT $6.12/LB — DOWN 6% IN JUNE AS FED HAWKISHNESS BITES; SECTION 232 REFINED COPPER REPORT DUE WHITE HOUSE TODAY
snippet: Copper futures settled near US$6.12 per pound at the June 26 weekly close — down 6.2% for the month despite holding 21% above year-ago levels — as hawkish Federal Reserve signals dampened near-term industrial metals demand expectations and reduced the probability of rate cuts that had supported commodity prices earlier in the year. The end of Q2 coincides with the June 30 deadline for the Commerce Secretary to submit a refined copper market report to President Trump, after which the White House may impose a phased universal duty of 15% on refined copper imports starting January 1, 2027 and 30% starting January 1, 2028 — a decision that would materially improve the economics of North American copper producers and advanced U.S.- and Canadian-jurisdiction copper explorers.

headline: IF GOLD REBOUNDS TO $4,700 — MINERS WOULD POST THE RICHEST CASH FLOW QUARTER IN HISTORY: THE LEVERAGE MATH (GOLDSEEK)
snippet: A recent GoldSeek analysis argues that if gold recovers to US$4,700 per ounce from its current ~$4,028 level — a recovery of less than 17% — gold mining companies operating at all-in sustaining costs of $1,400–$1,600 would generate operating margins and free cash flow yields that would represent the richest earnings environment in the sector's recorded history. The case for equities over physical bullion at current gold prices rests on asymmetric leverage: a modest gold recovery translates into a far larger percentage gain in producer cash flows and net asset values, particularly for companies whose AISC is locked in through multi-year cost structures, making the current correction a potential entry window for quality producers that would otherwise be priced for $5,500 gold.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE IS FLIPPING LITHIUM FROM SURPLUS TO DEFICIT — ESS DEMAND SHARE TO HIT 31% IN 2026 AS SPODUMENE HOLDS $2,260/T
snippet: Mining.com's analysis of the lithium market finds that energy storage system deployment is emerging as the dominant marginal demand driver for lithium in 2026, with ESS expected to represent approximately 31% of global lithium carbonate equivalent demand — up from 23% in 2025 — as hyperscaler data center build-out and grid storage deployment accelerate simultaneously. With Australian spodumene concentrate (6% Li₂O, CIF China) holding near US$2,260 per tonne as of late June, and analysts at BMI, S&P Global, and Sprott now projecting a surplus-to-deficit transition in H2 2026, beaten-down lithium juniors with development-stage hard-rock assets in established jurisdictions may be approaching a fundamental re-rating catalyst before project economics fully reflect the structural demand shift.
